name: Koddelta Catalog Feed and Tag for Pinterest
author: koddelta

sections.description:
Put your WooCommerce products on Pinterest and see which Pins sell, without a login that keeps disconnecting.

Most Pinterest plugins ask you to connect your Pinterest account through a login window. When that connection fails, expires or is not offered in your country, your catalog stops updating. Koddelta Catalog Feed and Tag for Pinterest skips that step. It writes your catalog to a feed file that Pinterest fetches on its own, and it adds the Pinterest Tag with nothing more than your Tag ID.

What problem does it solve?

  • Your catalog sync broke and you do not know why.
  • You cannot tell which Pins or ads lead to real sales.
  • Pinterest rejects products and you only find out after uploading.

Who is it for?

Small and medium WooCommerce stores that want Shopping Pins, a Pinterest catalog and conversion tracking without a developer, a monthly app or a Pinterest login inside WordPress.

How it works

  1. Paste your Pinterest Tag ID and website claim code.
  2. Tick “Generate the feed file” and save.
  3. Add the feed URL in Pinterest under Catalogs > Data sources.

The “Getting started” tab inside the plugin walks you through these steps with links to the right Pinterest pages.

Features (free)

  • Product catalog feed for Pinterest, refreshed daily or hourly in the background.
  • Pinterest Tag (pixel) with checkout events, loaded after cookie consent when a WP Consent API plugin is active.
  • Status page: feed health, last run, product count and the products Pinterest would reject, each with an edit link.
  • Website claim tag support.
  • No Pinterest account connection: you paste a Tag ID, nothing is linked or authorised. The plugin itself does not track your store; the optional Pinterest Tag and Save button load Pinterest scripts (see External services).

Free and Pro

The free version covers everything above. Pro adds extra feed and tag options for stores that want more control; see the Upgrade link inside the plugin for details.

External services

This plugin works with Pinterest services. It does not send any data to the plugin author.

1. Pinterest catalog feed. The plugin writes a CSV file in your uploads folder. Pinterest downloads that file from the URL you give it in your Pinterest account. The plugin does not contact Pinterest for this; Pinterest requests the file, and your server answers it with the product data in the feed (title, description, price, image and product links).

2. Pinterest Tag (only when you enter a Tag ID). The plugin loads the Pinterest Tag script from s.pinimg.com on your store pages. The script, running in the visitor’s browser, sends the Tag ID, the page address, the visitor’s IP address and browser details, and checkout events (for example order value and currency) to Pinterest (ct.pinterest.com). It is needed for conversion tracking. When a WP Consent API plugin is active, nothing is loaded until the visitor accepts marketing cookies. Service provided by Pinterest, Inc.: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

3. Pinterest Save button (only when you turn it on). The plugin loads pinit.js from assets.pinterest.com on product pages. Your visitor’s browser contacts Pinterest to show the Save button, which sends the page address and the visitor’s IP address and browser details to Pinterest. Same provider and links as above.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress go to Plugins > Add New, search for “Koddelta Catalog Feed and Tag for Pinterest”, install and activate. WooCommerce must be active.
  2. Open WooCommerce > Feed & Tag and follow the setup steps on the page.
  3. Paste your Pinterest Tag ID and the website claim code, tick “Generate the feed file” and save.
  4. Copy the feed URL and add it in Pinterest under Catalogs > Data sources.
sections.faq:
Why is there no “Connect to Pinterest” button?

Account connections are the most common reason Pinterest catalog plugins stop working: expired tokens, blocked callbacks, accounts that will not link, unsupported countries. A feed is just a file that Pinterest downloads, and the Tag needs only its ID, so there is nothing to disconnect.

Does it work in my country?

The plugin itself has no country restriction. Whether Product Pins and shopping ads are available depends on your Pinterest business account and region.

How do I give the feed URL to Pinterest?

Copy the feed URL from WooCommerce > Feed & Tag. In Pinterest open Ads > Catalogs (or Business hub > Catalogs), choose “Create data source”, paste the URL, choose CSV and your currency, and set a daily update.

Where do I find my Tag ID?

In Pinterest Ads Manager open Conversions, then Tag manager. The Tag ID is the long number shown there.

How do I claim my website?

In Pinterest open Settings > Claimed accounts > Websites > Claim, choose “Add HTML tag” and copy it. Paste it into the “Website claim” field and save, then click Verify in Pinterest.

A product is missing from the feed. Why?

The status page lists the products that were left out and why: no image, no price, not published, hidden from the catalog, out of stock, or a variable product without variations. Each one has an edit link.

Pinterest says my Tag is unhealthy or sees no conversions. What do I check?

Open WooCommerce > Feed & Tag Status. The Pinterest Tag section shows whether a Tag ID is set, whether a consent plugin is holding the Tag back, and when the last checkout event was sent. Place a test order and check it with the Pinterest Tag Helper browser extension.

Pinterest could not validate my feed.

The status page checks the feed first and tells you why it would fail: no products, file missing, not updated, or most products skipped. Fix the listed products and press “Generate now”.

How often is the feed updated?

Daily or hourly, your choice. You can also press “Generate now” on the status page at any time.

Will it slow down my store?

No. The feed is built in the background in small batches, using Action Scheduler when available. The Tag script loads asynchronously.

Does it respect cookie consent?

Yes. If a consent plugin that supports the WP Consent API is active, the Pinterest Tag only loads after the visitor accepts marketing cookies. Developers can also use the fatp_tag_allowed filter.

Can I use it together with another Pinterest plugin?

Use only one plugin for the Pinterest Tag, otherwise events are counted twice. Turn the Tag off in the other plugin or leave the Tag ID empty here.

Can I change the feed address?

Yes. The status page has a button that creates a new address and deletes the old file. Update the URL in Pinterest afterwards.

short_description: Pinterest product catalog feed and Pinterest Tag (pixel) for WooCommerce. No account login to break: paste your Tag ID, add the feed URL, done.
